threats.residual_limit: deterministic identity prevents caller-chosen aliases for the represented binding but does not authenticate who requested persistence or prove the historical binding itself is legitimate
canonical candidate validation prevents alternate interpretations of the supplied object but cannot prove the original event snapshot was truthfully produced by an authorized actor
binding to the supplied active policy prevents self-consistent policy-digest forgery inside the candidate but does not establish governance approval for changing that policy
the inert contract checks the caller-supplied expected head against historical structure; live atomic compare-and-set against durable Grid state is still a promotion blocker
classification is deterministic once the existing Grid event is supplied, but this slice does not yet perform the durable event lookup or append transaction itself
prefix binding keeps retries stable as represented histories extend; it does not prove omitted history never existed or that an externally supplied prefix is globally complete
the contract separates ephemeral signed-request freshness from durable event identity, while live durable conflict handling still depends on future Grid integration
reusing the Grid evidence chain avoids a second persistence authority, but a Circle-specific durable head projection and concurrency check are not activated in this contract

the receipt records supplied successful chain-verification evidence and signature presence; this inert helper does not independently call the Grid verifier or cryptographically verify the signature object
a durable Grid record can establish that AXIOM stored a specific historical binding candidate; it does not prove consent, quorum, legitimacy, legal authority, execution authority, or truth
this slice defines and validates the admission object only; it does not persist Circle records through the running Grid service and must not be advertised as live Circle persistence
